e-web-push.1.evidence: Settings > Web Push has no Enable box (2.0.7: Extensions page only); it shows the auto-generated VAPID public key, Default Notification Title and Notification Icon URL. Saving a valid icon -> "Web Push settings saved."; the VAPID key option stayed the same across saves. A bad icon "not-a-url" -> "Notification Icon was not changed: it must be an http:// or https:// image address. The previous value was kept. Your other changes were saved."

e-web-push.2.evidence: Re-read line, guest: GET /jetonomy/v1/push/vapid-key -> 200 {public_key} only (no private key in the body); GET /push/service-worker.js -> 200 application/javascript; charset=UTF-8 with Service-Worker-Allowed: /

e-web-push.3.evidence: needs a live push service and a real browser permission grant; none is available on this stack

e-web-push.4.evidence: bob POST /push/subscribe {endpoint (fcm.googleapis.com), p256dh, auth} -> 201 subscribed true created true; the same again -> created false and one row only; DELETE /push/subscribe -> unsubscribed true. Note the body takes flat p256dh/auth (not keys{}); an endpoint on an unknown host such as push.example.test is refused as invalid

e-web-push.15.evidence: Re-read line: `wp jetonomy-pro web-push vapid-key` prints public_key and is_configured 1, `count` prints 0 active subscriptions; but `subscriptions --user=10` errors 'missing --for parameter' (the real flag is --for) and `send` takes --to, not a positional user. Looks like a stale check line; `subscriptions --for=10` answers 'No rows.'

e-web-push.16.evidence: Web Push switched off: /push/service-worker.js -> 404 and the subscription row inserted beforehand was kept (count 1); switched back on -> 200
